title: Camera capture and photo upload from a phone
when: Users take or pick photos on a phone and upload them; full size photos are too heavy, rotate wrong or fail on weak signal.
prompt:
Goal: A photo picker that opens the camera, shrinks and re-encodes the image on the device, and uploads it with progress and retry.
Steps:
1. <label for="photo">Add photo</label><input id="photo" type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment">; drop capture to let users choose the gallery.
2. On change read file = input.files[0]; reject files over 25 MB and types not starting with "image/".
3. Decode with createImageBitmap(file, { imageOrientation: "from-image" }) so rotation from the camera is applied.
4. Draw onto a canvas scaled so the long side is at most 1600 px, then canvas.toBlob(cb, "image/jpeg", 0.8); re-encoding also drops GPS EXIF data.
5. Show a preview with URL.createObjectURL(blob) and revoke it when replaced.
6. Upload with FormData through XMLHttpRequest so xhr.upload.onprogress can drive a <progress> element; set a timeout and offer retry.
7. When offline, save the blob in IndexedDB and send it later.
8. Some phones deliver HEIC files; if decoding fails, upload the original and let the server convert.
Quality bar:
- Uploads are usually under 500 KB.
- The photo appears upright in the preview and on the server.
Pitfalls:
- Reading the whole file with FileReader into a data URL, which uses far more memory.
- Leaking object URLs on every pick.
- Keeping location EXIF data the user did not mean to share.
Verify:
- [ ] The input has a label and accept="image/*".
- [ ] Resize caps the long side.
- [ ] Progress and retry work on throttled network.
Output: photo.js, the input markup and upload progress styles.

examples.input: usuario tira foto pelo celular e envia pro sistema, mas fica muito pesado
examples.output: capture input, createImageBitmap with orientation, 1600 px JPEG 0.8, XHR progress and retry
